transcript.text: Could you make a promo for Northside Gym with a welcoming gym scene rather than hardcore bodybuilding? I want people to feel comfortable about the idea of going to the gym, because I know it can feel a little intimidating at first. I’m probably overthinking how it will come across, but that’s why I’m explaining it all. It should have upbeat music and no voiceover, and what I’m after is a 10-second vertical video. For the last 5 seconds, please keep all these details on screen together: “Northside Gym”, “18 Cedar Road”, “Mon–Fri 6am–10pm”, “Sat–Sun 8am–6pm”. Make that text big enough to read on a phone.

Your Northside Gym promo is done: 10 seconds, vertical (9:16), with upbeat music and no voiceover.

Download: http://127.0.0.1:8000/films/2e4f1140e63247fe9695a876b14e8406.mp4

What's in it:
- **0–5 s:** A bright, friendly local gym with daylight, plants and wood floors. Everyday members of different ages and body types work out at an easy pace and chat, and a staff member greets a newcomer with a high five. It's relaxed, not hardcore.
- **5–10 s:** A calm shot of the gym interior with all four lines on screen together, in large type: "Northside Gym", "18 Cedar Road", "Mon–Fri 6am–10pm", "Sat–Sun 8am–6pm".
- **Music:** Feel-good pop with acoustic guitar, claps and a light beat, under the whole video.

Please check the end before you post it. The text was drawn into the picture by the image generator, and I couldn't look at the frame myself, so I can't confirm the spelling of the address and hours. The free plan also makes video at 480p, so look at the text on your phone to make sure it's sharp enough.

If anything is wrong, I can redo the last 5 seconds as a plain colour background with the text added directly. That way the spelling is guaranteed and the text is very easy to read, but the gym won't be behind it.

This used 265 credits.
transcript.why: The reply presents a finished result: a 10-second vertical promo video with a download link and a description of its contents. It includes caveats about checking the on-screen text and the 480p quality, and it offers an optional redo. It does not ask a question, request approval, refuse, or say it cannot do the task. The offer to redo the last 5 seconds is an optional follow-up, not a wait for input.
